title: From Observation to Intervention: Memory in Brains and Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.12377v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Brains and large language models (LLMs) are fundamentally different memory systems, but they can be compared through shared functional questions: where memory-related information is represented, how partial cues recover broader associations, how new information is written or updated, and how memory-related states can be perturbed. In biological systems, these questions span synapses, neuronal ensembles, hippocampal-cortical interactions, and plasticity; in LLMs, they span weights, activations, context windows, retrieval systems, and external stores. The comparison is therefore functional and experimental rather than anatomical. Human studies reveal sparse concept responses, temporal binding, rapid association formation, episode-specific coding, and recall-related reactivation, but selective intervention remains limited. translated_title: 从观察到干预：大脑与大型语言模型中的记忆
translated_abstract: 大脑和大型语言模型（LLMs）是根本不同的记忆系统，但可以通过共享的功能性问题进行比较：记忆相关信息在哪里表示，部分线索如何恢复更广泛的关联，新信息如何写入或更新，以及记忆相关状态如何被扰动。在生物系统中，这些问题涉及突触、神经元集群、海马-皮层相互作用和可塑性；在LLMs中，它们涉及权重、激活、上下文窗口、检索系统和外部存储。因此，这种比较是功能性和实验性的，而非解剖性的。人类研究揭示了稀疏概念响应、时间绑定、快速关联形成、事件特定编码和回忆相关再激活，但选择性干预仍然有限。啮齿动物研究提供了对学习相关集群更具选择性的因果访问，而人类和猕猴干预...
tldr: 本文通过功能性问题框架，系统地比较了大脑和大型语言模型在记忆表示、关联恢复、信息更新和干预方面的异同，强调了从观察到干预的跨系统研究视角。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically compares memory systems in brains and large language models through a functional framework, highlighting similarities and differences in representation, association recovery, updating, and intervention, with an emphasis on moving from observation to causal manipulation.
